05-crossfilter-flight-explorer.visual_critic_note: Intentional dark theme with a coherent sky-blue accent, meaningful bar color encoding (default/filtered/dimmed), clean typographic hierarchy, and stripped axes — genuinely designed, though the charts occupy only the top third of the viewport leaving a large empty void below.
05-crossfilter-flight-explorer.encoding_integrity_note: Zero-baseline bars, data-driven Y-domain via d3.max, correct crossfilter height updates, no area/dual-axis violations; hardcoded X-domains are domain-appropriate and an unused maxCount variable is the only minor code quality issue.
05-crossfilter-flight-explorer.stress_test_note: The brush 'brush' event calls updateAll() on every mousemove with no debounce/RAF, triggering full data filter+rebin across all 3 charts at 60fps; reset's clearBrush() fires brush 'end' events that recurse into updateAll() once per chart; no touch/mouse event filtering is present.
05-crossfilter-flight-explorer.cognitive_load_note: Three linked histograms with a single monochromatic palette and clear brush interaction — well within working memory limits, no color overload, and the hint text removes ambiguity about interaction model.

08-small-multiples-seasonal.visual_critic_note: Intentional dark theme and coordinated 3-color palette elevate it above generic defaults, but the lower third of the viewport is dead space and 9px axis labels at #404050 are borderline illegible.
08-small-multiples-seasonal.encoding_integrity_note: Zero baseline correct (y0=y(0), domain starts at 0), shared data-driven Y scale across all panels enables honest comparison, no lie factor or dual-axis issues; mild CatmullRom smoothing is appropriate for daily data with no missing values.
08-small-multiples-seasonal.stress_test_note: Every mousemove fires updateCrosshairs() which synchronously mutates DOM attributes across all 12 panels plus rebuilds tooltip innerHTML with no debounce, throttle, or requestAnimationFrame coalescing; no touch event handling or sourceEvent filtering exists.
08-small-multiples-seasonal.cognitive_load_note: 12-panel SPLOM-style grid with shared y-axis and 3 perceptually distinct year colors reads as a single conceptual unit; panels are large enough to distinguish line patterns, and the synchronized crosshair aids comparison without adding visual clutter.

11-zoomable-treemap.visual_critic_note: Deliberate dark theme with per-directory color coding and depth-based darkening shows real design intent, but 8 saturated categorical colors together feel visually heavy and typographic hierarchy is minimal — overall a competent developer-tool aesthetic that stops short of polished.
11-zoomable-treemap.encoding_integrity_note: Treemap area encoding is mathematically honest (d3.treemap sums file sizes into proportional rectangles, no lie factor), colors are categorical per directory, and key functions are present, though the remove-then-rejoin pattern on every render undermines object constancy.
11-zoomable-treemap.stress_test_note: Resize handler fires render() on every event without debouncing; rapid clicks during 300ms enter transitions have no .interrupt() guard, though click-based (not brush/zoom) interactions avoid most update-storm and stale-closure risks.
11-zoomable-treemap.cognitive_load_note: Single-view treemap with 8 well-separated color zones and clear depth-shading keeps cognitive load low; small cells lose labels but that's expected at this density, and zoom interaction provides a natural drill-down escape valve.

16-sankey-energy-flow.visual_critic_note: Dark background combined with opacity 0.38 on the flow ribbons makes the core Sankey data encoding nearly invisible — the nodes are legibly colored but the flows connecting them are so faint that the diagram's primary purpose (showing relative flow volumes) is essentially unreadable.
16-sankey-energy-flow.encoding_integrity_note: Node heights are per-stage renormalized (each stage independently fills available height) while link widths use a global px-per-unit scale derived from stage 0, so links systematically overflow or underflow node boundaries at intermediate stages — a structural Sankey encoding violation, though proportionality within each dimension is otherwise honest.
16-sankey-energy-flow.stress_test_note: The drag handler calls recomputeLinks() on every mousemove — recomputing all link geometries and updating all path `d` attributes with no throttling, debounce, or requestAnimationFrame coalescing; no other interaction traps (transitions, dispatch loops, stale scales, touch conflicts) are present.
16-sankey-energy-flow.cognitive_load_note: Stage headers and labels orient clearly, but the flow ribbons are nearly invisible at 0.38 opacity on a dark background, collapsing the Sankey into disconnected colored columns and hiding the energy-flow narrative the chart is built to show.

17-chord-diagram-trade.visual_critic_note: Screenshot captures the animation mid-flight — chord ribbons (the core data encoding) are invisible and country labels haven't appeared yet, leaving only a plain colored ring that communicates nothing about trade flows; the intentional dark palette and custom colors are wasted on a chart that reads as broken at render time.
17-chord-diagram-trade.encoding_integrity_note: Chord layout correctly encodes arc width proportional to trade values via d3.chordDirected(), tick marks are data-driven (k = angleSpan/value), tooltip math is accurate, and no baseline/area-scaling/dual-axis issues apply; screenshot appears captured mid-animation before chord ribbons faded in, but structural encoding is honest.
17-chord-diagram-trade.stress_test_note: The animDone guard uses the D3v5 (d,i,nodes) signature on a D3v7 transition.on('end') which receives (event,d), so nodes is undefined and animDone is never set true, permanently locking out all hover interactions; no brush/zoom means no Update Storm, Stale Scale, or Infinite Loop risk, and no touch filtering is present but the interaction surface is hover-only.
17-chord-diagram-trade.cognitive_load_note: Screenshot captured mid-animation (arcs only, no chords or labels rendered), limiting full assessment; the final state with 90 directed chords across 10 colors (above the 8-hue warning threshold) will be dense, but hover-isolation and staged transitions are well-designed mitigations.

23-hex-bin-map.visual_critic_note: Intentional dark-navy + YlOrRd palette creates a striking, harmonious look with good typographic hierarchy, though subtitle and legend labels (#3d444d) are nearly invisible against the dark background.
23-hex-bin-map.encoding_integrity_note: Color encoding is data-driven via d3.max with no area-scaling deception, but linear normalization on heavily skewed metro-population data compresses most bins toward the cool end of the ramp, limiting perceptual discrimination in low-density regions.
23-hex-bin-map.stress_test_note: The slider `input` event calls `render()` synchronously on every tick with no debounce or RAF coalescing, triggering a full hexbin recomputation and canvas redraw on every mousemove during drag; no other interaction traps are present (no transitions, no cross-view dispatch, no touch/mouse conflict).
23-hex-bin-map.cognitive_load_note: Single-view hex density map with sequential color ramp, one adjustable parameter, and a tooltip — minimal cognitive load; the warm-on-dark palette encodes density intuitively and the gradient legend is immediately scannable, though the subtle color range between low and mid-density bins requires close inspection.

35-color-palette-explorer.visual_critic_note: Deliberately designed tool with intentional warm-neutral background, clean typographic hierarchy, restrained palette selector UI, and a well-structured three-panel layout — the WCAG contrast matrix is genuinely useful and visually polished, though the contrast matrix labels are quite small and the CVD swatches feel slightly oversized relative to the bar chart panel.
35-color-palette-explorer.encoding_integrity_note: Bar chart correctly starts at zero with a semantically appropriate [0,100] domain for percentage data and no size-encoding or dual-axis violations, but the hardcoded domain and absent key functions in data joins are minor robustness gaps.
35-color-palette-explorer.stress_test_note: The resize handler fires renderBarChart() and renderContrastMatrix() on every resize event without debouncing or RAF coalescing; all other interaction paths (palette clicks, tooltip mousemoves) are either infrequent or DOM-cheap, and no brush/zoom/cross-view dispatch creates loop or stale-scale risks.
35-color-palette-explorer.cognitive_load_note: Three views (bar chart, 7×7 contrast matrix, 4-row CVD strips) form a coherent analytical unit with clear hierarchy; the matrix is information-dense but color-coded bands and tooltips manage it well, and palette-switch updates all three simultaneously without disorientation.

39-quadtree-hit-detection.visual_critic_note: Dark-themed particle demo with deliberate GitHub-palette UI, satisfying glow/connector interaction feedback, and clean legend — slightly undermined by the static screenshot showing dense overlapping clusters that blur together without the mouse interaction active.
39-quadtree-hit-detection.encoding_integrity_note: No quantitative size encoding avoids lie factor; position and color are the only channels and both are correct; hardcoded N=5000 is a demo constant, not a domain clamp, and quadtree rebuilds from data on every zoom so scaling/subset relations hold.
39-quadtree-hit-detection.stress_test_note: mousemove and zoom handlers synchronously call rebuildScreenPoints(), kNearest(), and draw() on every event with no RAF coalescing or dirty-flag deferral, iterating 5000 canvas points at 60fps; the voronoiDirty flag is a positive pattern but the core render loop is unthrottled.
39-quadtree-hit-detection.cognitive_load_note: 5,000 points across 8 well-separated clusters with a restrained dark palette; the nearest-neighbor highlight with glow and connector lines gives clear interactive focus, though 8 categorical colors is at the warning threshold and the Voronoi overlay could add visual noise if enabled simultaneously.

41-force-bundling-chord-triptych.visual_critic_note: Deliberately designed dark-theme triptych with cohesive 5-color palette, clean panel divisions, and intentional cross-panel linking — held back from 8 by the radial panel's cramped, rotated node labels that are difficult to read at this size.
41-force-bundling-chord-triptych.encoding_integrity_note: Relational/topological charts with no bar/area baseline violations; chord correctly uses proportional arc angles and data-driven matrix, but cross-panel highlight maps node hover to group-level ribbons (overstating connections) and link stroke-width uses linear scaling for value rather than a perceptually correct channel.
41-force-bundling-chord-triptych.stress_test_note: Hover correctly uses mouseenter (no update storm or stale-scale risk), no D3 transitions so no mid-flight snap, and no feedback loop; however drag on force nodes has no touch-event filter and the dispatch omits a source parameter, leaving a theoretical re-entry path if handlers were ever extended.
41-force-bundling-chord-triptych.cognitive_load_note: Three linked panels with 40 nodes and 5 categories stay within working memory limits; the dim-on-hover interaction elegantly manages cross-panel complexity, though the radial bundling center shows noticeable tangle for cross-group edges that can't be fully assessed without live interaction.

47-mixed-scale-parcoords.visual_critic_note: Dark-theme parallel coordinates with intentional color palette, canvas/SVG hybrid for performance, good typographic hierarchy with scale-type badges, and satisfying brush interaction — slightly generic categorical colors prevent it from reaching 8.
47-mixed-scale-parcoords.encoding_integrity_note: Data-driven domains via d3.extent throughout, appropriate log scale for salary with clearly labeled scale-type badges per axis, and canvas rendering avoids DOM join key-function concerns — structurally honest with no baseline, lie-factor, or dual-axis fabrication issues.
47-mixed-scale-parcoords.stress_test_note: Brush handler calls draw() synchronously on every mousemove without RAF or debouncing, re-rendering 300 canvas polylines per frame; no touch event filtering on the brush.
47-mixed-scale-parcoords.cognitive_load_note: 300 lines at 0.62 opacity on canvas keeps active traces readable, but convergence at the two ordinal axes (Department, Performance) creates dense fan patterns that obscure individual paths until brushing is used.

49-textured-network-diagram.visual_critic_note: Thoughtful dual-encoding concept (color + texture for accessibility) with a cohesive dark palette, but the force layout leaves the cluster off-center in the lower viewport with large dead space above, and the rightmost legend item (Zeta) is visually clipped.
49-textured-network-diagram.encoding_integrity_note: Categorical encoding (community → color + texture) is honest with no quantitative distortion — all nodes use fixed uniform radius (no lie factor), redundant dual-channel encoding supports accessibility, force center is dynamic, but no key functions on data joins and hardcoded simulation distances are minor robustness gaps.
49-textured-network-diagram.stress_test_note: No D3 transitions, no brush events, and no cross-view dispatch—interaction surface is minimal and clean—but the zoom handler lacks a `.filter()` to prevent simultaneous touch-drag and pinch-zoom conflicts on mobile.
49-textured-network-diagram.cognitive_load_note: 6 communities with dual color+texture encoding are distinguishable at a glance, but 50 nodes packed into a dense central cluster with no visible community separation makes community membership hard to parse without hovering.

51-accessible-force-network.visual_critic_note: Dark-mode GitHub-inspired palette with clear community color coding and thoughtful focus/selection states, but the network edges are nearly invisible against the background and the bottom data table is cut off, leaving the layout feeling incomplete at render size.
51-accessible-force-network.encoding_integrity_note: Node radius is encoded linearly (r = 4 + degree/maxDeg * 5.5) rather than with scaleSqrt, introducing a mild area lie factor, but maxDeg is correctly data-driven and no baseline, dual-axis, or gap-handling issues apply to this chart type.
51-accessible-force-network.stress_test_note: The mousemove listener runs an unthrottled O(n) linear hitTest scan over all 150 nodes on every event to update cursor style, but no brush/zoom storms, no D3 transitions (eliminating mid-flight snap), no cross-view dispatch (no infinite loop risk), and no touch handlers (no mouse-touch fight).
51-accessible-force-network.cognitive_load_note: 150 nodes with near-invisible edges at rest keeps the network readable, but two perceptually similar red-orange community colors (Cassini #f78166 / Fenrir #ff7b72) undermine the primary categorical encoding and will be indistinguishable for most viewers.

52-accessible-choropleth.visual_critic_note: Clean YlOrRd palette and readable layout work well, but the legend is undersized and unlabeled with actual values, the subtitle doubles as an accessibility disclaimer rather than adding insight, and the overall presentation is functional but unremarkably generic.
52-accessible-choropleth.encoding_integrity_note: Sequential color scale uses data-driven domain (d3.min/d3.max), no quantile trap, table bars correctly encode from zero, and the legend gradient faithfully maps the full data range — minor point that the color domain starts at minVal (2.1%) rather than 0 is acceptable and standard for choropleths.
flags: Update Storm (unthrottled d3.geoContains loop over all features on every mousemove with no RAF/debounce)
Mouse-Touch Fight (no touch event handling or synthetic-event filtering)
52-accessible-choropleth.stress_test_note: Hit-testing runs O(n) geo contains on every mousemove without throttling, and the absence of any touch event guards risks double-trigger on mobile; no transitions or cross-view dispatch loops are present.
52-accessible-choropleth.cognitive_load_note: Single sequential color scale (YlOrRd) across 51 states reads immediately — high/low regions pop without effort, the legend is minimal and clear, and the info panel surfaces precise values on demand rather than cluttering the map.

79-reduced-motion-dashboard.visual_critic_note: Intentional dark theme with a restrained monochromatic blue palette and decent typographic hierarchy, but the three charts occupy only the top half of the viewport leaving a large dead zone, and the 'dark dashboard with single blue accent' treatment is a well-worn template rather than a distinctive design choice.
79-reduced-motion-dashboard.encoding_integrity_note: Zero baselines on all bar/histogram charts, data-driven y-domains, scatter Y truncation is acceptable for position-encoded dots, and crossfilter scales correctly stabilize under filtering; minor issue is the hardcoded age X domain [20,67] which could clip out-of-range data.
79-reduced-motion-dashboard.stress_test_note: Both brush handlers fire on every mousemove via '.on("brush end", ...)' calling updateAll() (full DOM mutations on all three charts) at 60fps with no debouncing, RAF, or throttling; additionally no .interrupt() is called before new transitions are started, risking mid-flight snaps during rapid brushing.
79-reduced-motion-dashboard.cognitive_load_note: 3 crossfiltered views with a single monochromatic palette, clear filter pills, and labeled axes keep cognitive load low; the scatter's 400 overlapping dots at small size are the only readability strain.

82-hive-plot-accessible.visual_critic_note: Deliberately designed dark-theme hive plot with a colorblind-safe palette, clear typographic hierarchy (uppercase tracking on axis labels, muted tick/legend chrome), restrained edges at 0.18 opacity, and a balanced four-corner UI layout — but the chart sits slightly high in the viewport leaving dead space below, and the dense edge bundle at center is visually muddy until hover interaction resolves it.
82-hive-plot-accessible.stress_test_note: No brush/zoom/transitions so most traps are N/A; the only issue is the ResizeObserver calling full svg.selectAll('*').remove() + render() on every resize tick without debouncing, which can cause a DOM-rebuild storm during window drag-resize.
82-hive-plot-accessible.cognitive_load_note: Single-view hive plot with 5 perceptually-distinct colors and low-opacity edges (0.18) manages 80-node/120-edge density well, though the center edge convergence creates a visual blob that obscures individual connection paths without hover interaction.

83-community-detection-table.visual_critic_note: Deliberately designed dark-theme split-panel with harmonious Tableau palette consistently applied across hulls, nodes, table headers, and bar sparklines, though the force graph clusters in a fraction of the left panel leaving conspicuous dead space at top and bottom.
83-community-detection-table.encoding_integrity_note: scaleSqrt used correctly for node-size encoding, betweenness bars are zero-based with data-driven normalization, hull joins use a key function — no lie factor, no truncated baselines, and no silent gaps; node joins lack a key but the visualization is static so no object-constancy violation occurs in practice.
83-community-detection-table.stress_test_note: updateHulls() performs a full D3 data join and hull recomputation on every simulation tick (~60fps) with no requestAnimationFrame coalescing or dirty-flag guard, causing excessive DOM mutations during drag interactions; no brush/zoom stale-closure or infinite-loop risks exist, and no explicit touch event filtering is present but D3 drag handles basics.
83-community-detection-table.cognitive_load_note: 5-color palette and convex hull boundaries keep 100-node force layout readable; graph+table split gives spatial overview plus ranked detail without exceeding working memory limits.

87-skill-anatomy-treemap.visual_critic_note: Dark background with deliberate per-category color palette, clear group-label hierarchy, and generous padding give the treemap a polished, intentional feel — held back slightly by some cells truncating to cryptic initials and the rightmost column being clipped ('META · WORKSH…').
87-skill-anatomy-treemap.encoding_integrity_note: Treemap correctly encodes data as proportional area via d3.treemap().sum(d => d.lines), data-driven layout with no hardcoded domains, no baseline or radius-deception issues; minor deductions for synthetic data and missing key functions (mitigated by full re-render on resize).
flags: Update Storm (ResizeObserver calls full svg.selectAll('*').remove() + rebuild on every resize event without debounce/RAF)
Update Storm (pointermove sets tooltip innerHTML on every mouse move without throttling)
87-skill-anatomy-treemap.stress_test_note: No zoom/brush/transitions to mishandle, and pointer events avoid mouse-touch fights, but the un-debounced ResizeObserver triggers a complete DOM teardown and rebuild on every resize frame.
87-skill-anatomy-treemap.cognitive_load_note: 10 categories with perceptually distinct colors, 29 leaf cells, dark group backgrounds cleanly separate sections, and label truncation prevents clutter — the treemap reads as a coherent structure at a glance with no overwhelming density.

98-shape-morphing-timeline.visual_critic_note: Cohesive dark theme with monospace typography, restrained blue palette, and a well-designed scrubber control, though the single flat bar color and minimal typographic contrast between title and subtitle keep it from feeling truly polished.
98-shape-morphing-timeline.encoding_integrity_note: Zero baseline and area fill are correct, but y-domain is hardcoded at [0,110] rather than data-driven via d3.max, and data joins lack key functions — structurally honest but brittle to data changes.
flags: Update Storm - scrubber input handler calls render() directly on every mousemove in parallel with the always-running RAF loop, producing double renders per scrub frame without dirty-flag coalescing
98-shape-morphing-timeline.stress_test_note: No D3 transitions are used (manual RAF interpolation eliminates mid-flight snap and stale-closure risks), but the scrubber input event fires render() unthrottled alongside the perpetual RAF loop, doubling DOM mutations during scrubbing.
98-shape-morphing-timeline.cognitive_load_note: Single view with one color and a clear sequential morph sequence keeps cognitive load very low; the scrubber labels and type badge orient the viewer throughout, though animation quality cannot be fully assessed from a static screenshot.
